# `synthetic-liveness` — the two ends of a stall's life

**HAND-MADE, NOT CAPTURED.** Every session here is generated by
`scripts/make-stall-fixtures.mjs` and says so in its slug directory name
(`SYNTHETIC-hand-mutated-not-captured`), its `cwd` (`C:\SYNTHETIC`) and its own message text. G6
applies: nothing in this tree was observed on anyone's machine, and no test may quote it as
evidence about what Claude Code does.

Added for v0.7.0 Phase 0c, DoD 0c.5.

## Why it exists

The harvested corpus `fixtures/cc-2.1.260/…/99f96635-…` is the real evidence for stall detection,
and it has one gap that matters: **it contains a stall that never resolved, and no tool that
stalled and then RECOVERED.** A rule that promotes a tool to `stalled` and can never take it back
would pass every assertion that corpus can make.

So these two isolate the ends:

| case | the result | what it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `stall-then-resume` | **arrives**, 5 minutes past the threshold | `running` → `stalled` → `done`, with no reset path called |
| `stall-until-ended` | **never arrives** | stays `stalled` — silence is not an outcome |

`stall-until-ended` is the one worth stating plainly. A tool whose session has gone quiet must not
be quietly promoted to `done` or `error`: we do not know how it ended, or whether it did. Resolving
it would be exactly the guess G3 forbids, and it is the failure mode a "tidy up stale nodes" change
would introduce while looking like housekeeping.

## The pair is a pair, and a test asserts that

The two files differ **only** in whether the third line exists, and in the session id — which must
differ so both can be registered in one model. `src/model/stall.test.ts` normalises the ids and
compares the shared prefix line by line, so the contrast above really does isolate the result's
arrival rather than some other incidental difference.

## Why generated rather than hand-typed

The timestamps ARE the content. A hand-typed set that drifts by a second stops testing the boundary
it was written for, silently. `scripts/make-stall-fixtures.mjs` declares the offsets once:

| offset from `2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z` | meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0` | session start |
| `1,000` | the tool call — and the session's last observed activity |
| `121,000` | exactly `lastActivity + 120,000`; must **not** be stalled |
| `121,001` | one millisecond past; must be stalled |
| `421,000` | `stall-then-resume` only: the result lands |

`120,000` is `agentDeck.livenessThresholdMs`, quoted from the existing liveness setting and never
redefined here. Regenerate with `node scripts/make-stall-fixtures.mjs`; the script clears the tree
first, so the corpus is a function of the script rather than of its own history.

The version on every line is `2.1.260`, deliberately **in-window**: these must be ACCEPTED by the
fingerprint. A refusal fixture that quietly becomes acceptable does not fail, it passes while
testing nothing — the trap `synthetic-layout/07` and `08` have been re-versioned twice for — and
these are not refusal fixtures.

## What this corpus does not prove

- **Nothing about real Claude Code behaviour.** It is hand-made. The real evidence that a tool can
  stop for a quarter of an hour and never return is the harvested `99f96635-…` session, and the
  nesting it shows (a stalled child implying a stalled parent spawn) is not modelled here at all —
  both cases are single-agent by design, so the recovery arm is not entangled with the join.
- **Nothing about any other engine.** OpenCode and Codex tool-completion shapes are their own
  question.
- **Nothing about the threshold's VALUE.** These pin the boundary's direction — `= threshold` is
  not stalled, `> threshold` is — not that 120 s is the right number for a person.
